name: Ad blocker detection
plain: Creates bait elements to see whether an ad blocker hides them.
meaning: Shows when someone uses content blockers, which also marks privacy tool users.

web.api: Create .adsbox style elements and read offsetHeight

limits.headline: Can guess whether you use an ad blocker, by checking if its bait ads vanish
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Check if a hidden bait element gets hidden or blocked
Show a message asking you to turn off your blocker
Count how many visitors use blockers
cannot: See which blocker you use for sure
See your browser history or other add ons
Turn your blocker off for you
Be exact; privacy tools can fool the check
limits.reach_label: A guess when the page loads

story.what_it_is: A site can quietly test whether you use an ad blocker.
story.for_you: You never see the test. If it finds a blocker, you may get a message asking you to turn it off, a paywall or a block on the page.
story.for_makers: Publishers do it to protect ad income and to push people to subscribe. Fraud and tracking tools also use it, because a blocker marks someone as a privacy tool user and adds to a device fingerprint.

use_cases.example: A news site shows 'Please turn off your ad blocker or subscribe' after the test.
A free video site stops playing until you allow ads.
A free browser game site shows an ad wall and counts blocked ads.
An ad network measures how many people block ads to know its true reach.
A fraud tool treats a blocker as one more signal in a device profile.
A publisher reports how many readers block ads in its audience stats.
